# Command reference

JSON mode writes one stable envelope to stdout and is the default when stdout is not a TTY. Text, raw, and help output are explicitly selected exceptions. The `inspect` commands use an explicit `--profile` or the saved read default; `operator-write snapshot`, `prepare`, `apply`, and `reconcile` use an explicit profile or the saved write default. Explicit flags override defaults; empty flags and stale saved identities fail closed. Auth, profile administration, project policy, and native mutation retain explicit-profile requirements. No-profile `capabilities` remains build-only; local operator status does not consult defaults. Configure selection with `profile defaults show|set|clear`. See `contract.md` for exit codes and envelopes.

## JSON response recovery

Apply this grammar in order:

1. A v1 envelope is exactly one complete top-level JSON object followed only by
   whitespace. It requires boolean `ok` and a JSON integer `v` whose value is
   exactly `1`. Decimal, exponent, string, null, boolean, and every other
   version representation is unsupported. If `ok` is `true`, `data` must be
   present and non-null; `error` and `hint` must be absent, and their presence
   is invalid even when `null`. If `ok` is `false`, `data` must be absent;
   `error` must be a present non-null object with string `code` and `message`,
   and `hint` must be a present string. Forbidden-key presence is invalid even
   when `null`. `meta` is optional; unknown additive fields are tolerated. They
   never repair an invalid known member. On either branch, `meta` may be absent;
   when present it must be a non-null object and may be empty. Every present
   known metadata member must
   be non-null and have its exact v1 type: `count` is a nonnegative JSON integer
   written without a fraction or exponent, `truncated` is boolean, and
   `next_cursor`, `profile`, `instance`, `account_id`, and `account_login` are strings. Unknown additive metadata
   members are tolerated, but they never repair a missing, null, or wrongly
   typed known member. A malformed `meta` makes the entire envelope invalid. A
   valid v1 envelope is the primary result; never replace it with stderr. Any
   malformed or unsupported envelope
   makes stdout invalid.

   Valid v1 examples:

   `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{},"future":true}`

   `{"ok":false,"v":1,"error":{"code":"PROFILE_REQUIRED","message":"profile is required","future":true},"hint":"pass --profile","meta":{"count":0,"truncated":false,"next_cursor":"","profile":"work","instance":"https://example.youtrack.cloud","future":null},"future":true}`

   Invalid examples:

   - `{"ok":true,"v":2,"data":{}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1.0,"data":{}}`
   - `{"ok":"true","v":1,"data":{}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":"1","data":{}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":null}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"error":null}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"hint":null}`
   - `{"ok":false,"v":1,"hint":"stop"}`
   - `{"ok":false,"v":1,"error":null,"hint":"stop"}`
   - `{"ok":false,"v":1,"error":{"code":1,"message":"failed"},"hint":"stop"}`
   - `{"ok":false,"v":1,"error":{"code":"FAILED","message":1},"hint":"stop"}`
   - `{"ok":false,"v":1,"error":{"code":"FAILED","message":"failed"},"hint":1}`
   - `{"ok":false,"v":1,"error":{"code":"FAILED","message":"failed"},"hint":"stop","data":null}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":null}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":[]}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"count":null}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"count":-1}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"count":1.0}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"count":1e0}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"count":"1"}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"truncated":null}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"truncated":"false"}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"next_cursor":null}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"next_cursor":1}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"profile":null}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"profile":false}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"instance":null}}`
   - `{"ok":true,"v":1,"data":{},"meta":{"instance":[]}}`

2. A valid v1 stdout envelope is authoritative; stderr is diagnostic only.
3. If a confirmed `mutation apply` result is missing, malformed, or reports
   `WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, never replay the mutation. Run the bounded
   `mutation reconcile` flow for the same receipt. An inconclusive result is
   `operator_resolution_required`, never inferred success or failure.

4. For `operator-write apply`, missing/malformed output or
   `WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` also forbids replay or an automatic equivalent
   new plan. Use `operator-write status` and GET-only `operator-write reconcile`
   for the same plan ID. `WRITE_APPLIED_LOCAL_FAILURE` means verified remote
   success with a local failure: do not resend. Operator confirmation is an
   explicit assertion, not a native receipt; the separate native `mutation`
   confirmation/apply/reconcile path remains unavailable.

## Global flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | bool |  | preview a supported local or offline change |
| `--fields` | stringSlice |  | comma-separated output fields |
| `-o, --output` | string |  | output format: text, json, or raw |
| `--profile` | string |  | explicit named YouTrack profile; overrides a saved default on supported commands |
| `--timeout` | duration | `30s` | abort the command after this duration |
| `-v, --verbose` | bool |  | write redacted request activity to stderr |
| `--yes` | bool |  | confirm a supported local configuration change or exact operator-write intent |

### `youtrack-agent-cli operator-write snapshot`

Read one exact issue or project and freeze a supported write target

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--clear-field` | stringArray |  | exact field name to leave empty at creation; repeatable, only with --kind issue.create, never with --clear-value or --field-id. The project field must allow empty values (canBeEmpty). A user field also needs the issue-create-user-fields capability |
| `--clear-field-id` | stringArray |  | immutable project custom-field ID to leave empty at creation; repeatable, only with --kind issue.create, never with --clear-value or --field |
| `--clear-value` | bool |  | empty the selected field instead of setting a value; only with --kind issue.update and exactly one --field or --field-id, never with --value or --value-id. The field must allow empty values (canBeEmpty) and currently hold one |
| `--comment-id` | string |  | immutable exact comment ID for comment.delete |
| `--direction` | string |  | exact link phrase read from the source issue, for example "depends on" or "is required for"; case-sensitive, never fuzzy |
| `--field` | stringArray |  | exact field name, for example Stage or Assignee; repeatable for issue.create, last wins otherwise |
| `--field-id` | stringArray |  | immutable project custom-field ID; repeatable for issue.create, last wins otherwise |
| `--file` | string |  | local regular file to attach; only with --kind attachment.add |
| `--id` | string |  | exact issue entity or readable ID for issue.update, issue.edit, issue.link (the source), comment.add, comment.delete, or attachment.add |
| `--kind` | string |  | supported write kind: issue.create, issue.update, issue.edit, issue.link, comment.add, comment.delete, or attachment.add |
| `--link-type` | string |  | exact issue link type name for issue.link; use --link-type-id when names repeat |
| `--link-type-id` | string |  | immutable issue link type ID for issue.link |
| `--name` | string |  | upload file name for attachment.add; defaults to the file's base name |
| `--out` | string |  | new exclusive 0600 snapshot path in an existing private directory |
| `--project` | string |  | exact project entity ID or key for issue.create |
| `--target-id` | string |  | exact target issue entity or readable ID for issue.link |
| `--value` | stringArray |  | exact target bundle value name, or exact user login for a user field, paired with --field |
| `--value-id` | stringArray |  | immutable target bundle value ID, or user ID for a user field, paired with --field-id |
